summary.headline: The week came in ahead of target on both orders and revenue, but the year is still behind target and the cancellation rate rose for a third week.

points.what: Orders reached 1,098, or 103.4% of the weekly target, and gross revenue reached $79,107, or 105.9% of target.
points.so_what: Both weekly targets were met, but one week above target does not close the year-to-date shortfall.

points.what: Revenue rose 8.7% week on week and 86.6% on last year, against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growing faster than the rate built into the targets is what is holding the quarter ahead of target.

points.what: The cancellation rate was 16.8%, up 2.2 pp on the week, a notable move in a bad direction and the third consecutive rise.
points.so_what: A third straight increase means the cancellation trend is not reversing.

points.what: The cancellation rate has now risen three weeks in a row, from 14.1% to 16.8%, with each percentage point worth $951 of revenue.
points.so_what: Every further percentage point costs close to a thousand dollars of weekly revenue against the target.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is $1,840,990 against a target of $1,856,700, or 99.2%, a gap of $15,710.
points.so_what: The year remains behind target despite the quarter running ahead.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target needs $85,326 of revenue a week for the remaining 24 weeks, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $74,142.
points.so_what: The rest of the year requires a step up from the current pace for the full-year target to stay within reach.

points.what: Orders finished at 103.4% of the weekly target, 36 orders above it, and revenue at 105.9%, $4,373 above it.
points.so_what: The week added to the buffer the quarter is carrying rather than drawing it down.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 115.1% of target, $29,825 ahead, with $760,112 of the $987,996 full-quarter target still to come over 10 weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter's lead has been built in three weeks, and the large majority of the quarterly target is still outstanding.

points.what: Year-to-date attainment stands at 99.2%, with four months behind target (Jan to Apr) and May, Jun and Jul MTD ahead.
points.so_what: The recent run of months above target has narrowed but not yet erased the shortfall from the start of the year.

points.what: APAC placed 491 orders, contributing 23 of the week's 29 additional orders, or 79.3% of the change.
points.so_what: Most of the week's order growth rests on one region, leaving the total sensitive to APAC alone.

points.what: Search placed 757 orders, contributing 30 orders, or 103.4% of the week's change.
points.so_what: Search accounted for more than the entire net increase, so gains there were partly offset elsewhere.

points.what: Organic fell 15.0% to 170 orders, a contribution of -30 orders.
points.so_what: Organic's decline offset the gain from Search and held the total increase to a modest one.

points.what: AOV was $86.65, up 8.7% on the week but 3.5% below the same week last year.
points.so_what: Basket size is below last year's level, so revenue growth of 86.6% trails order growth of 97.1%.

points.what: New signups were 231, down 0.4% on the week and 10.8% on last year, while orders rose 2.7% to 1,098.
points.so_what: Signups are the one customer-growth measure moving in a bad direction in a week that was ahead of target on orders.

points.what: The cancellation rate ran 1.5 pp above the same week last year, rated bad on both the weekly and yearly comparison.
points.so_what: Cancellations are above both last week's and last year's level, so the rise is not a one-week blip against a soft comparison.

points.what: Orders of 1,098 were above the 8-week average of 1,013 and outside the 8-week range.
points.so_what: The order level is running above recent weeks, which is what carried the week past its target.

summary.headline: Week ahead of target on orders and revenue, but the year is still behind at 99.2% of target with a rising cancellation rate.

points.what: Orders reached 1,098, 103.4% of the weekly target, and revenue reached $79,107, 105.9% of target.
points.so_what: Both weekly targets were met, adding to the quarter's cushion.

points.what: YTD revenue stands at $1,840,990 against a target to date of $1,856,700, or 99.2% attainment, status behind.
points.so_what: Strong recent weeks have not yet closed the shortfall built up earlier in the year.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose to 16.8%, a notable move of +2.2 pp and the third consecutive rise in the bad direction.
points.so_what: The trend is not reversing, which puts a growing share of placed orders outside revenue.

points.what: Orders and revenue were both outside their 8-week range, with orders up 97.1% and revenue up 86.6% on last year against the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth is running ahead of the rate the targets were built on.

points.what: The cancellation rate has risen for three straight weeks, from 14.1% to 16.8%, and each percentage point is worth $951 of revenue.
points.so_what: Every further point of cancellation removes close to a thousand dollars from the week's revenue.

points.what: YTD revenue is behind target at 99.2%, and hitting the full-year target of $3,888,802 requires $85,326 a week against a recent 8-week run-rate of $74,142.
points.so_what: The required pace sits well above the current pace, so the full-year target is out of reach without a step up in weekly revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Jun 2026 was 9.9%, up 1.1 pp and rated bad both week on week and year on year.
points.so_what: More of the orders already counted in revenue are coming back, which weakens the quality of the reported growth.

points.what: QTD revenue is $227,884 against a target to date of $198,059, or 115.1% of target, with $760,112 still needed over the remaining 10 weeks to reach the full-quarter target of $987,996.
points.so_what: The quarter has a healthy cushion after three weeks, but most of the quarterly target is still ahead.

points.what: Orders came in 36 above the weekly target and revenue $4,373 above it.
points.so_what: The week added to target attainment on both measures rather than drawing on the quarter's cushion.

points.what: Four months of the year finished behind target (Jan to Apr) while May, June and July MTD are ahead.
points.so_what: The year-to-date gap is a carryover from the first four months rather than a feature of recent trading.

points.what: APAC orders rose 4.9% to 491 and contributed 23 of the weekly order increase, 79.3% of the change.
points.so_what: The region holding 44.7% of orders is also where almost all the weekly growth came from.

points.what: Search orders rose 4.1% to 757, contributing 30 orders, 103.4% of the total change.
points.so_what: Without Search the week's order growth would not have happened.

points.what: Organic orders fell 15.0% to 170, a contribution of -30 orders, while Display rose 80.0% to 54.
points.so_what: Display's gain offset the Organic decline, so the order total held up despite a large drop in one source.

points.what: AOV rose 8.7% week on week to $86.65 but remains 3.5% below last year, rated bad year on year.
points.so_what: Revenue growth on last year is coming from more orders rather than bigger baskets.

points.what: The cancellation rate reached 16.8%, above last year's 15.3% by 1.5 pp.
points.so_what: Order quality is weaker than a year ago even as volume grows strongly.

points.what: New signups were 231, down 0.4% week on week and down 10.8% on last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Signups are moving in the opposite direction to the 97.1% order growth.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 29 Jun 2026 was 9.9%, against 8.8% the week before and 8.8% last year.
points.so_what: Returns sit above both the recent and prior-year level, a second quality measure moving the wrong way alongside cancellations.
